questions.question: CI on PR #1189 is red on every test lane, and the cause is not this PR. The newly released pytest-asyncio warns that asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope is unset, and filterwarnings=error turns that into an INTERNALERROR at configure time. I reproduced it locally. Master went green at c58ee74 only because that run was earlier, and the next master run will fail the same way. The fix is one line in pyproject.toml, asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function". No async fixture is wider than function scope, so behaviour stays the same. No fix PR exists. Where should it go?

options.label: Separate fix PR, port here (Recommended)
options.description: I file a BUG item and open a small PR on a new branch (needs your OK to push a second branch), then port the same line into #1189. That port does nothing once master has it. Master gets fixed on its own, and #1189 can go green and start its review loop.

options.label: Only in this PR
options.description: I add the line plus a CHANGELOG/BUG entry to #1189 as a co-shipped fix. That's one branch, but the PR grows past BK-498 and master stays red until #1189 merges.

options.label: Wait for a master fix
options.description: I post the failing check and the proposed patch as a PR comment and start the review loop on red CI. The loop can't close until master carries the fix and this branch merges it in.

BUG-345 merge order. Rounds 1, 3 and 4 each flagged that PR #1189 cites BUG-345 in pyproject.toml comments and in its trace, while BUG-345's backlog entry lives only in PR #1190 (still open). If #1189 merges first, master cites an ID nothing defines until #1190 lands. How should this be settled?

options.label: #1190 first, then sync (Recommended)
options.description: You merge #1190 first. I then merge master into #1189, which removes the duplicate pyproject change and makes BUG-345 resolve, and the closing round runs on that state. #1189 waits on #1190.

options.label: Drop the ID from #1189
options.description: I strip BUG-345 from #1189's pyproject comments and trace, keeping only the setting and pin. Either PR can merge first, but merging the second one will give a small pyproject conflict to resolve.

options.label: Accept the window
options.description: Leave it as is. The PR body already states "merge #1190 first", and I resolve the thread as accepted. If the order slips, master briefly cites an undefined ID.

questions.question: One subject-list row can't be covered from this container: a real cloud worker restart after /clear, the incident's actual trigger. It's covered only by the unit path (disarm on clear, then rearm on resume, with a tested marker) and by the earlier probe showing disarm runs on /clear. Waive it for this PR?

options.label: Waive, bound stated (Recommended)
options.description: Close with this row waived and the reason recorded in the Step 5 report: the restart can't be reproduced on demand, and its hook-side effect is pinned by tests. The next real /observe session is the live check.

options.label: Probe again first
options.description: Before closing, you trigger a worker restart after /clear in a throwaway /observe session, and I check the marker survives as a release. This costs your time, and a restart isn't reliably triggerable.
